Routing notes:
- Option C (regional office) was rejected for every tested request, regardless of request type, size, region, requester department, or wording. Do not select C based solely on regional origin or mention of a regional office.
- Option B (priority desk) succeeded for REQ-2409: a small north-region shipment where the client had asked twice already. This supports using B for repeated/urgent follow-up, but evidence is limited to one case.
- Tested request categories included refunds, shipments, and claims across north, south, and east regions; no reliable mapping to A, B, or D has been established beyond the successful B case.
- Requester department and submitter name did not provide a validated routing rule.
- Treat phrases such as “second attempt,” “before end of day,” and repeated client inquiries as possible priority signals; prefer B when urgency is clear, while recognizing this is not yet fully confirmed.
- Avoid assuming that “regional office” in the requester’s note means option C.

Routing notes:
- Option C (regional office) remains unsupported and has been rejected in prior tests. Do not choose C merely because a note mentions a regional office.
- Option B is not a general urgency rule. It succeeded for REQ-2409 (small north shipment, repeated client inquiry) and REQ-2410 (small east invoice, second attempt), but failed for REQ-2417 (small south shipment, second attempt) and REQ-2419 (small south claim, before end of day). Treat urgency/repetition as a possible signal, not sufficient evidence.
- Option A succeeded for small south refunds in REQ-2411 through REQ-2414, including both “no rush” and “regional office” wording. This supports A for comparable small south refunds.
- Option A failed for small north claims (REQ-2415 and REQ-2416) and a large east invoice (REQ-2418). “Regional office” and “scanned, not typed” did not make A valid in those cases.
- Request type, size, and region appear relevant, but no complete mapping to A, B, or D is established. In particular, invoices, shipments, and claims with urgency wording have produced mixed outcomes.
- Requester department and submitter name remain unvalidated routing signals.
- Prefer previously validated exact or near-exact patterns; otherwise avoid confident assumptions and continue treating A/B/D as uncertain.

Routing notes:
- Option C (regional office) remains unsupported and has been rejected in prior tests. Never choose C merely because “regional office” appears.
- Option D is also weak/invalid in recent cases: rejected for a large north claim (REQ-2421), large north shipment (REQ-2422), and small south claim (REQ-2425). Do not infer D from requester department or region.
- Option A is validated for small south refunds (REQ-2411–2414) and now for large refunds from the north (REQ-2420) and south (REQ-2423–2424). “Same as last month,” urgency, or repeated inquiry may accompany successful A, but are not sufficient alone.
- Option B is pattern-dependent. It succeeded for large and small north shipments on a second attempt (REQ-2426–2427), a small east shipment with end-of-day urgency (REQ-2428), REQ-2409, and REQ-2410. It failed for a small north refund on a second attempt (REQ-2429), as well as REQ-2417 and REQ-2419. Repetition/urgency is only a possible signal.
- A failed for small north claims (REQ-2415–2416) and a large east invoice (REQ-2418); “regional office” and “scanned, not typed” did not rescue those cases.
- Request type, size, region, and perhaps exact wording appear relevant, but no complete A/B/D mapping exists. Invoices, shipments, claims, and urgency language remain mixed.
- Requester department and submitter name remain unvalidated routing signals.
- Prefer validated exact or near-exact patterns. Otherwise avoid confident assumptions; treat A/B/D as uncertain and continue gathering evidence.

Routing notes:
- C (regional office) remains unsupported. Never choose C merely because “regional office” appears.
- D (external partner) remains unsupported and has been rejected in prior cases. Do not infer it from department or region.
- A is validated for small south refunds, large north/south refunds, and a small east refund with repeated inquiry (REQ-2433). However, A failed for small/large claims in north and south, a large east invoice, and a small north refund even when “regional office” was mentioned (REQ-2436). Do not generalize A from refund patterns or urgency/repetition.
- B is validated for shipments: large north with “regional office” (REQ-2430), small north with “same as last month” (REQ-2437), and prior north/east shipment cases. B also succeeded for a large east invoice with end-of-day urgency (REQ-2438) and a small north claim with no-rush wording (REQ-2435).
- B failed for a small east claim with end-of-day urgency (REQ-2431). Thus urgency is only a possible signal, not sufficient; claims remain mixed.
- A failed for a large south claim with urgency and a large south claim mentioning scanned paperwork (REQ-2434, REQ-2439), reinforcing that wording does not override request-type patterns.
- Request type, size, region, and exact wording appear relevant, but no complete A/B mapping exists. Refunds currently favor A; shipments often favor B; claims are inconsistent. Invoices are mixed.
- Requester department and submitter name remain unvalidated routing signals.
- Prefer validated exact or near-exact patterns. Otherwise avoid confident assumptions; treat A/B as uncertain and continue gathering evidence.

Routing notes:
- C (regional office) and D (external partner) remain unsupported. Never infer either from region, department, or wording.
- B is strongly validated for shipments, including large north (“no rush,” REQ-2445), and for invoices: small north with end-of-day urgency (REQ-2444) and large east with “same as last month” (REQ-2447). Prior shipment validations remain valid.
- B is validated for a small north claim with “let me know if anything is missing” (REQ-2448), but claims otherwise remain mixed or B-negative: large east claims failed with “same as last month” (REQ-2440) and repeated inquiry (REQ-2446); large south claims failed with end-of-day urgency (REQ-2442); small south failed with “no rush” (REQ-2441). Do not generalize B across claims.
- A remains validated for several refunds, but failed for a large east refund even with neutral wording (REQ-2443). Refunds therefore favor A in some patterns, not universally.
- B failed for a small south invoice despite repeated-inquiry wording (REQ-2449); invoices are mixed, though B is now validated for north/east examples.
- Existing A failures remain: multiple north/south claims, a large east invoice, and a small north refund; wording such as urgency, scanned paperwork, or “regional office” does not override request-type patterns.
- Request type, size, region, and exact wording all appear relevant. Requester department and submitter name remain unvalidated signals.
- Prefer validated exact or near-exact patterns. Otherwise mark A/B uncertain and avoid confident assumptions; do not let urgency, repetition, or “same as last month” decide alone.

Routing notes:
- C (regional office) and D (external partner) remain unsupported. Never infer either from region, department, submitter, or wording.
- B is strongly validated for shipments in several patterns: large north (“no rush”), east small (“regional office”), and prior shipment cases. However, B failed for a small south shipment despite repeated-inquiry wording; do not generalize across regions.
- B is validated for invoices including small north (scanned paperwork), large east (“same as last month” and “regional office”), and likely small east with repeated inquiry because A failed. Invoices remain mixed; exact pattern and region matter.
- A is no longer supported for the newly tested refunds: it failed for large south with repeated inquiry and second attempt, small south with “no rush” and with missing-information wording, and small east with missing-information wording. Earlier A refund successes remain, but refunds are highly pattern-dependent; do not assume A.
- Existing A failures remain for multiple claims, a large east invoice, and a small north refund. Urgency, repetition, scanned paperwork, “regional office,” or “same as last month” do not independently decide routing.
- Request type, size, region, and exact wording all appear relevant. Requester department and submitter name remain unvalidated signals.
- Prefer validated exact or near-exact patterns. Otherwise mark A/B uncertain; do not confidently choose C/D or let one wording cue override request-type and regional evidence.

Routing notes:
- C (regional office) and D (external partner) remain unsupported. Never infer either from region, department, submitter, or wording.
- B is validated for shipments in several exact/near-exact patterns: large north (“no rush”), small east with “same as last month,” “second attempt,” and “no rush,” and prior shipment cases. Do not generalize B to other request types.
- B is validated for invoices including small north with repeated inquiry, scanned paperwork, and prior cases; small east with scanned paperwork; and large east (“same as last month”/“regional office”). Invoice routing remains pattern- and region-dependent.
- B has now failed repeatedly for claims: small east (“no rush”), small south (urgent, “regional office”), and large south (repeated inquiry). Do not choose B for claims absent stronger evidence.
- A is unsupported for many tested refunds: large south repeated inquiry/second attempt; small south “no rush,” missing-information, and scanned-paperwork wording; small east missing-information; plus earlier small north failure. Earlier A refund successes remain, so refunds are highly pattern-dependent and generally uncertain.
- Existing A failures remain for multiple claims and a large east invoice. A/B cannot be selected confidently for unvalidated patterns.
- Urgency, repetition, scanned paperwork, “regional office,” and “same as last month” are not independently decisive; their effect depends on request type, size, and region.
- Request type, size, region, and exact wording all matter. Requester department and submitter name remain unvalidated signals.
- Prefer validated exact or near-exact patterns. Otherwise mark A/B uncertain; do not confidently select C/D or let one wording cue override the combined evidence.
